purpose: Upgrade the first operator-comparison research group with reusable passage context, paired sequences and explicit interpretive limits without assigning new evidence strength.

project_sequence: care/support is described as carrying or stabilizing
the supported person regains breathing/movement capacity
mature care aims toward walking and independent capability rather than permanent carrying
biblical_sequence: Israel is recalled as a child called from Egypt
YHWH teaches Ephraim to walk and takes them in the arms
healing and feeding accompany care
rebellion introduces judgment
compassion complicates total destruction
correspondences: care directed toward life rather than possession
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The full Hosea context keeps the useful developmental-care analogy while adding an important restraint: parental tenderness is embedded in a covenant relationship of grief, freedom, failure and compassion, not a mechanical authority formula.

project_sequence: the project asks when support should stop substituting for another's movement
release is framed as part of successful care rather than abandonment
biblical_sequence: Israel is found and guarded in wilderness
eagle imagery stirs the nest and hovers
wings catch and carry the young
YHWH leads and provides
the poem later contrasts care with Israel's forgetting
correspondences: support that is not the final state
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Reading the whole Song prevents the eagle image from becoming a simplistic 'push them out of the nest' rule: protection, leading, carrying and provision all remain active parts of the metaphor.

project_sequence: a person/entity is modeled as more than an object
the figure can function relationally as Door/Way/connective path
access then becomes infrastructure linking otherwise separated states or rooms
biblical_sequence: Hebrews develops priesthood and sacrifice
confidence to enter the holy place is announced
a new and living way is associated with Jesus and the curtain/flesh image
the community is told to draw near, hold fast and encourage one another
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The passage gives a strong textual example of person-to-access-path language, but its full context also shows that the path exists inside a specific Christological, priestly and communal argument rather than as a generic law of information architecture.

project_sequence: the House contains differentiated rooms or members without erasing relation
biblical_sequence: alienated groups are brought near and reconciled
through Christ both receive access
access is in one Spirit
the destination is the Father
people become household
joined construction grows into temple/dwelling in Spirit
relation_argument.why_it_matters: This is one of the clearest biblical passages for testing the project's relational Trinity/House architecture because the roles remain grammatically differentiated while participating in one access-and-dwelling chain.

project_sequence: later Seat/throne language represents established authority or integrated order
biblical_sequence: a prophetic sign-act centers on a crown and priest
the Branch is announced
the Branch grows
builds YHWH's temple
bears glory
sits/rules on a throne
priestly and royal relations are held together
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The oracle is unusually valuable because sprouting, building and enthronement occur in one textual unit; at the same time, its post-exilic temple setting sharply limits any claim that a modern seed→house→seat sequence fulfills Zechariah.

project_sequence: centralized carrying is treated as useful in some phases
mature systems distribute function and responsibility
connected parts increasingly support growth through their own contribution
biblical_sequence: unity of the body is affirmed
different gifts and roles are given
leaders equip rather than perform every function
saints perform ministry
the body matures
supporting connections join the body
each part works and contributes to growth
correspondences: equipping rather than permanent central carrying
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The full Ephesians passage improves the systems analogy by showing that distribution is not fragmentation: differentiated contribution remains coordinated by shared unity, maturity and a head/source.
